label: run
message:
The new renderer exposes mine positions during play and misrepresents the board after a loss. Timer lifecycle bugs also leave the clock running after play or navigation ends.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Hide mine sprites while the game is in progress — C:\Users\19161\saolei\entry\src\main\ets\common\GameController.ets:199-201
  After the first tap places mines, every covered mine satisfies `cell.mine` and is drawn on the board. This exposes the mine locations during play. Render mine sprites only for states that should reveal them.

- [P2] Render revealed mines after a loss — C:\Users\19161\saolei\entry\src\main\ets\common\GameController.ets:188-194
  When a mine is hit, `lose()` marks every unflagged mine as revealed, but this branch draws a mine only when `cell.exploded` is true. The other mines disappear or appear as numbers on the loss board. Handle revealed mine cells here as well.

- [P2] Draw the misflag overlay on covered cells — C:\Users\19161\saolei\entry\src\main\ets\common\GameController.ets:190-192
  When a player loses with a flag on a safe cell, `lose()` sets `misflagged` but leaves that cell unrevealed. The red-cross drawing code is reachable only for revealed cells, so incorrect flags remain visually indistinguishable from correct ones.

- [P2] Stop the timer when the game ends — C:\Users\19161\saolei\entry\src\main\ets\common\GameController.ets:272-277
  If a tap wins or loses after the timer has started, `tap()` redraws without stopping the interval. The displayed time continues increasing after the result, and the callback keeps running indefinitely. Stop it when `reveal()` leaves the engine in `Won` or `Lost`.

- [P2] Clear the game timer when the canvas disappears — C:\Users\19161\saolei\entry\src\main\ets\components\MinefieldCanvas.ets:56-58
  If the user leaves the page during an active game, `aboutToDisappear()` clears only the long-press timeout. The controller's interval retains the controller and continues drawing to a detached canvas. Stop that interval during component teardown.
